## E2 - capture fidelity (edge drops and conservative read windows)

Model, stated plainly: (a) *precise capture with missing edges* drops each
DERIVED_FROM edge independently with probability d (one draw stream per seed, so a
higher rate always drops a superset of the edges); (b) *conservative read-window
capture* gives every write its true parents plus up to K carried-over reads from the
same modelled session (docs/01 section 7.3 "last K READ targets"; 5 actions per
session). E2 is a model of capture
error, not a measurement of real runtime coverage. E6 is NOT MEASURED: one genuine installed OpenCode read-hook shape is verified, but there is no labeled coverage or benign-friction corpus.

## E4 - latency (real FalkorDB, real engine calls)

One throwaway graph per size, built through the engine, then the real engine
timed over rounds (the real revoke uses a different root per round, because a
second revoke of the same root is idempotent by design). `build_ms` is the
per-node write path through the engine, not a bulk loader - reported as-is.

## E3 - scenario replay through the HTTP API

`evals/run_e3.py` (also `tests/evals/test_e3_scenarios.py`) POSTs every
authored `demo/scenarios/*.json` node through `/v1/events`, attests the
corroborations with the operator credential, revokes the root through
`/v1/revoke` and asserts the fixture's expected statuses plus gate verdicts: the
high-risk push built on the revoked branch is never `allow`, and a private tag
reaching a public audience is `block` with its path.
Trusted human/scanner support attestation requires the operator credential under the source-identity/trust ADR-008; arbitrary MCP agent claims do not grant that authority.

## E5 - scoped isolation and concurrency verification

Current local verification covers three integration tests in `tests/integration/test_isolation_concurrency.py`: the API isolation matrix, threaded tenant stress with invariant checks, and revoke-during-ingest consistency. These tests do not prove absence of all isolation or race defects.
The optional database ACL mechanism test in `tests/security/test_acl_mechanism.py` is skipped without its deployment secret. The service still uses a shared administrative database connection; wiring per-tenant database credentials into the running service remains open. A separately configured ACL mechanism is not proof of that service boundary.

## E6 / E3b - NOT MEASURED

The 2026-10-16 free-only installed OpenCode recheck captured one genuine read-tool before/after hook shape. Its final response timed out; this is payload-shape evidence, not a labeled coverage or benign-friction corpus. The current S1/S8 demo is synthetic. The recorded-session experiment and live-agent video remain planned work.

## E4b - FalkorDB vs SQLite traversal (honest answer)

Same closure/ancestor queries in FalkorDB (`algo.BFS`, over the socket) and in
stdlib `sqlite3` (`WITH RECURSIVE`, in-process) on the same generated DAG, with
the descendant and ancestor ID sets asserted equal. Scope: the traversal primitives only - not the
revoke pipeline. The measured traversal timings are reported below; conclusions apply
only to these rows and this host (the graph query pays a round-trip). What FalkorDB
provides this implementation is one graph per tenant, `GRAPH.COPY` for an isolated what-if, and
database ACLs. SQLite can also support logical isolation; this benchmark does not compare those architectures.

| nodes | edges | closure_nodes | closure_sqlite_ms | closure_falkor_ms | ancestors_sqlite_ms | ancestors_falkor_ms |

| 820 | 1230 | 268 | 0.28 | 1.81 | 0.02 | 0.86 |
| 4100 | 6136 | 416 | 0.52 | 2.38 | 0.01 | 1.37 |
| 16400 | 24560 | 336 | 0.48 | 4.17 | 0.02 | 3.26 |

## Limitations (docs/03 section 7, verbatim)

## 7. Honest limitations (paste into README "Limitations")
- Pedigree **contains, explains and reverts**; it does not detect bad sources or prevent prompt injection.
- E1 has built-in ground truth: it quantifies baseline semantics, not lineage discovery. E2 is a model of capture error. E3 replays patterns, not the cited papers' experiments. E6 and benign friction are **NOT MEASURED**: one genuine OpenCode read-hook shape is verified, but there is no labeled runtime coverage or benign-friction corpus.
- Session read-window capture over-approximates influence (ratio reported); `cite` edges tighten it but depend on agent cooperation (tagged `agent_reported`).
- `preserved` is only as good as the corroboration signal. Under the source-identity/trust ADR-008, trusted human/scanner attestation over REST requires the operator credential; MCP agents can assert only agent-level corroboration. An arbitrary agent claim does not create trusted independent support.
- `preserved_correct` is explicit-status sensitivity, not retention or preservation precision; a baseline zero does not imply all supported items were discarded.
- E5 currently covers three isolation/stress/race integration tests. The optional DB ACL test is skipped without its deployment secret; the service still shares an administrative DB connection, so per-tenant database credential wiring remains open.
- Hooks see only what the runtime exposes; paraphrase laundering through an unhooked channel is invisible.
- Bash risk classification is heuristic. External effects (pushes already pulled, emails sent) are listed, not undone.
- Cloud Free: 100 MB, no TLS, no persistence - hosted demo uses synthetic data only; benchmarks ran locally.
- B0-B5 are emulations of semantics described in public docs/papers, not the vendors' products.

## How to reproduce

```bash
make eval          # full grid (N>=30 seeds per cell)
make eval-quick    # one cell, 2 seeds
```
